name: Ismael Wu
life: “I still remember addressing a letter to a father whose home had changed.” Saturday often includes a stop at the brick passage off the shop row, where Ismael takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I paid postage for the last copy. It is the first letter the girl's father will open in his new home.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a long navy raincoat and one cuff folded back twice. Ismael has one cheek that creases before the other, with short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak. Ismael gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in during a conversation.
personality: Ismael finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To deliver a letter to the father's current home.
family: Jody Gao is Ismael’s cousin raised in the same household. Ismael calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Jody leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The rescue hut mural*, Jody says, “I recognize the scar on her painted calf. My old teammate got it in the same meet I lost.”
connections: Albert Hsu. A bus number and a new home address help the final copy get where it belongs.
